name: Weight loss for chin definition
lead: Weight loss for chin definition refers to the idea that reducing body fat makes the chin and jawline look sharper by reducing fullness under the chin, often called a double chin. Wikipedia distinguishes two causes of a double-chin appearance: in some overweight people, subcutaneous fat around the neck creates a fold, while in others, often of normal weight, the jaw bones do not project far enough forward [1].

Wikipedia describes surgical fat removal for the first type and jaw or chin surgery for the bony type, but it gives no outcome data for either [1]. The pages reviewed do not address whether fat can be lost from the chin area selectively, and no study located for this entry tests weight loss as a way to change chin appearance.
infobox: Soft-tissue fat versus bony chin deficiency [1]

paras: According to Wikipedia, the soft-tissue form is attributed to excess subcutaneous fat around the neck, whereas the bone form occurs in people of normal weight when the jaw bones are insufficiently projecting, and the chin can appear to merge into the neck even at low body fat [1]. Wikipedia notes subcutaneous fat is distributed unevenly, with the number of fat cells varying by body area and their size changing with nutritional state [2].

Wikipedia lists surgical removal of the fat pad for the soft-tissue form and genioplasty or orthognathic surgery for bony deficiency [1], and describes chin augmentation by implants, sliding genioplasty and fillers [3].

card.summary: Losing body fat to reveal the chin and jawline; plausible where fullness is soft tissue, but no studies test it and bone structure is not changed.
card.note: Wikipedia notes a double-chin look can also come from bone structure, not fat.

quick.overview:
Weight loss for chin definition is the idea that lowering overall body fat reduces fullness under the chin and makes the jawline look sharper.

Wikipedia describes a double chin as arising either from soft-tissue fat or from jaw bones that do not project far enough; no study found here tests weight loss for chin appearance.
quick.mechanism: Reducing overall body fat shrinks fat cells, including those under the chin. The sources reviewed do not address whether fat loss can be targeted to one area.
quick.risks: The sources reviewed list no risks specific to this approach. When the cause is bone structure, fat loss is not described as changing the chin's projection.
